info.title: Trinity Customer Api
info.description:
## A Brief Overview.

The Trinity customer API is designed to allow customers to create, update, and view inspections. To request an inspection, you will provide us information about the project and type of inspection needed. After an inspection is received through the API Trinity's team will begin working the order like any other inspection. When the inspection is completed, a report will be generated and made available through the API. In addition to the report file, data such as budgets, documents, and photos are available to view. 

## Notes

The production environment can be accessed at api.trinityonline.com for non-production testing please use sandbox-api.trinityonline.com  Separate credentials are required per environment and can be obtained by providing the desired associated email to your customer success representative.
 
If you will be handling inspection for multiple lenders through a single set of API credentials please use the "Multi-Tenant" endpoints where available. 

All of your company's projects can be viewed through the API even if the projects were created using another method. 

We offer webhooks to allow updates to be pushed to your system. 

Most entity types support a "customerKey" property. This is an optional property that will allow you to tag an entity with a unique ID. This ID will not be shown anywhere in the UI and is explicitly designed to help you track the entities you create.

### For non-production environments
Orders are not worked automatically, if you would like an order to be worked during development please contact us with the Order ID you would like to have processed.


## Areas
| Area | Information |
|--|--|
| Authentication | Authentication is required for all endpoints within this API. Please use the API credentials provided by Trinity to redeem an API token. If you do not yet have API credentials, please reach out to Trinity to get started.
| Comments | Comments can be used to communicate with Trinity about orders and projects. 
| Companies | Provides a list of companies your API credentials have access to. Generally only needed for multi-tenant API users.
| Company Credit | Used to find company credit details before placing applicable orders.
| Documents | In some cases inspections require supporting documents to be uploaded to the API. The final report is also available in this area when an order is completed. 
| Report Results | For some form types we allow additional form results to be read via the api in additional to the report pdf.
| Forms | A form represents the type of inspection being requested. Not all form types are available to all customers in production. Each form has its own legal and contractual requirements that need to be handled outside of the scope of the API. These endpoints will only return the forms currently available.
| Budget | Holds budget information for an order. Not all inspection types require budget information. Look at the schema for each of the order endpoints to see if and what type of line items may be required.
| Order | An order represents a single inspection. It contains the information needed to complete that inspection such as the date and time the inspection should occur, priority of the inspection, and the analyst working the inspection. You will likely spend a majority of your time in this area and it's a good place to get started.
| Photos | Most inspection types include photos of the subject property. These photos are included in the final report but may also be retrieved directly through the API.
| Projects | A project contains one or more orders within. It contains details about the property, loan, and people. The information in a project will generally remain the same throughout a series of inspections. Projects are created and updated automatically as orders are made, but they can be updated independently in this area.
| Users | Users are also created automatically while using other endpoints, but in some cases, you may prefer to explicitly create and update user information. Please note users created in the API are created in an inactive state by default and cannot access the Trinity website.
| Webhooks | Webhooks allow our API to push updates to your integration. They are optional but recommended for the best experience.

## Basics to get started. 
#### Creating an inspection
To create an inspection, you will make a `POST` request to one of the endpoints with the following pattern `/api/v1.1/forms/{formId}/new` under the "Orders" section below. Each form type has different data requirements to create an inspection. Please check the schema for each endpoint. When creating the first inspection we will store information about the property, loan, contractor, and borrower to a project. If subsequent inspections are required, we will use the information provided from this request to look up the project and create a new order. If any of the information in the project changes, we will make relevant updates. If the type of inspection you are creating requires line items, they must be provided on the initial inspection. After the initial inspection you may provide the line items again, or if you provide a `null` value the line items will automatically be carried forward from the previous inspection. 

#### Getting inspection results
When an inspection is completed, a report document will be made available through the `/api/v1.1/orders/{id}/documents/report` endpoint. In addition to the report, you can also retrieve data such as invoices, line items, photos, and additional documents. 

#### Managing projects
As mentioned previously, projects are created and updated automatically when creating inspections. In some cases, updates need to be made to a project independently of order creation. To update a project, you can make a `PATCH` request to the `/api/v1.1/projects/{id}` endpoint. When making a patch request you should only include the properties you intend to update. If a null value is provided for a property, a default value will be used.

#### Querying entities
Projects, Orders, Comments, Documents, and Users can be queried useing OData filtering and paging. Page size is limited to 100 entities and some properties are not available for filtering. To learn more about OData filtering and paging please visit [the OData Documentation](https://docs.oasis-open.org/odata/odata/v4.01/odata-v4.01-part2-url-conventions.html#sec_QueryOptions).

#### Using Webhooks
If you would like to have data pushed to your integration we offer webhooks. To use webhooks create a `POST` request to the following endpoint `/api/v1.1/subscribe` with the url you would like the webhooks to be sent to and the type of events you want to subscribe to.
